+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

Index: src/main/resources/application.properties
===================================================================
--- src/main/resources/application.properties	
+++ src/main/resources/application.properties	
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+spring.application.name=demo
+
+# Default profile uses an in-memory H2 database so the app runs with zero setup.
+spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:demo;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;DB_CLOSE_ON_EXIT=FALSE
+spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
+spring.datasource.username=sa
+spring.datasource.password=
+
+spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
+spring.jpa.open-in-view=false
+spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.format_sql=true
+spring.jpa.show-sql=true
+
+spring.h2.console.enabled=true

parts.text:
The repo is essentially empty. I need to set up a new Maven Spring Boot Java project with JPA/Hibernate. Java/Maven aren't installed, but I can create all the project files. Let me plan the structure.

Let me ask no questions—the request is clear enough. I'll create a standard Maven Spring Boot project with:
- pom.xml with spring-boot-starter-parent, spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, a database driver (H2 for dev + note for postgres), spring-boot-starter-web maybe, test starter
- Main application class
- An example entity, repository, maybe a service/controller
- application.properties

Let me check that plugin file — maybe it's a trap/security guard. Let me read it to understand any restrictions.

1: const AUTH_STORE_RE = /\.local[/\\]share[/\\]opencode[/\\]auth\.json|opencode[/\\]auth\.json/i

4:   if (typeof args === "string") return AUTH_STORE_RE.test(args)
5:   if (Array.isArray(args)) return args.some(mentionsAuthStore)
6:   if (args && typeof args === "object") return Object.values(args).some(mentionsAuthStore)
